newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian shares end firm with Wall Street support.
newsitem.headline: Italian shares end firm with Wall Street support.

text.p: Italian shares ended firmed on Wednesday but off the day's highs supported by the higher opening to Wall Street and buoyed by the rise in domestic bonds and the lira, dealers said.

Stronger than expected U.S. first quarter GDP data put markets on hold as an early U.S. interest rate rise was seen more likely. But as Wall Street shook off the caution the Italian market followed suit. Trading was largely subdued ahead of Thursday's May Day holiday and a quiet day seen Friday.
The blue chip Mib30 index of top Italian stocks ended up 0.9 percent at 18,289, while the all-share Mibtel index was 0.93 percent firmer at 12,277.

Blue-chips largely up in line with the market with Pirelli 1.08 percent higher at 3,743 lire and Montedison rising 0.81 percent to 1,125, but Fiat bounded ahead up 2.76 percent at 5,660 in a further recovery from last week's losses.
San Paolo shares ended off 1.18 percent at 11,327 lire after the group warned of tough times ahead at its shareholders meeting to approve its privatisation plans.
Olivetti was one share to slip, off 0.14 percent at 497.9 lire, despite announcing a new chief executive at its Lexikon company and a management shake-up.

STET and Telecom Italia ended firmer after today's shareholders meeting in Turin approved the merger between the two state-controlled telecoms groups. STET up 0.99 percent at 8,126 lire and Telecom Italia up 1.12 percent at 4,533 lire.
